statement: The Earth orbits the Sun.
explanation: That's a fact: scientists have checked it with observations and calculations for centuries. A fact is something you can verify.

statement: Chocolate ice cream is the best flavor in the world.
explanation: That's an opinion! Different people like different flavors, and they're all correct about their own taste. Opinions are about preference, they can't be 'right' or 'wrong' like facts.

statement: Bats are blind.
explanation: That's a very common myth! Bats actually see just fine — they also use echolocation (sound) to get around in the dark. When you hear something surprising about animals, it's worth checking a book or asking an adult.

statement: Water boils at 100 degrees Celsius at sea level.
explanation: That's a fact you can test with a thermometer. Anyone, anywhere, gets the same result under the same conditions — that's what makes something verifiable.

statement: Adventure books are more fun than science books.
explanation: Opinion! It depends what each person enjoys reading. There's no single right answer — and it's fine to disagree with friends about this.

statement: An ad says a toy will 'make you the fastest kid at school.' How could you check if that's true?
explanation: Ads want to sell things, so they sometimes exaggerate. You can ask: 'Who said this? Is there proof?' Asking an adult or comparing it to what you already know helps you decide if it's a fact or just advertising.

statement: There are seven continents on Earth.
explanation: That's a geography fact you can confirm on an atlas or globe — many independent sources agree on the same number.

statement: Singing is more fun than drawing.
explanation: Opinion! Some people love singing, others prefer drawing. Neither answer is 'the right one' — it depends on the person.

statement: Plants make oxygen through photosynthesis.
explanation: That's a scientific fact, proven by experiments that anyone can repeat and get the same result.

statement: A video online shows a dog talking perfectly. Should you believe it right away?
explanation: Good thing to investigate! Very surprising things online can be edited, jokes, or even computer-made. Before believing or sharing, it's worth thinking 'does this actually seem possible?' and asking an adult.

statement: Portugal is located in Europe.
explanation: That's a geography fact — you can confirm it on any world map or atlas.

statement: Soccer is the most fun sport there is.
explanation: Opinion! Some people prefer swimming, dance, or basketball. Taste in sports differs from person to person.

statement: An AI chatbot answered a question and got it wrong. Can that happen?
explanation: Yes, it can! Computers and AI can make mistakes too, just like people. That's why it's always good to double-check important information with a book, a trusted adult, or another source.

statement: The adult human body has 206 bones.
explanation: That's a fact you can verify in science books and with doctors — the number stays the same when many sources confirm it.

statement: Spinach is the tastiest vegetable.
explanation: Opinion! Tastes are personal — what's delicious to some may not be to others, and that's perfectly fine.

statement: Honey never spoils if stored properly.
explanation: That's a fact! Archaeologists have found honey in Egyptian tombs thousands of years old that was still good to eat, thanks to its low water content and acidity.

statement: Eating carrots lets you see in the dark.
explanation: That's a myth! Carrots have vitamin A, which is good for your eyes, but they don't give you night super-vision. This myth became famous during World War II.

statement: Reading books is more fun than watching cartoons.
explanation: That's an opinion! Some people prefer reading, others prefer cartoons. There's no right answer — it depends on what each person enjoys.

statement: Octopuses have three hearts.
explanation: That's a fact! Two hearts pump blood to the gills, and the third pumps it to the rest of the body. You can verify it in marine biology books.

statement: If you swallow chewing gum, it stays in your stomach for 7 years.
explanation: That's a very widespread myth! Your body can't digest gum, but it passes through your digestive system like anything else that doesn't get digested, usually within a few days.

statement: Summer is the best season of the year.
explanation: That's an opinion! Some people love summer heat, others prefer winter cold or autumn colors. Preferences about seasons vary too.

statement: Portugal was the first country to reach India by sea from Europe.
explanation: That's a historical fact! Vasco da Gama reached India in 1498, sailing around Africa, and you can confirm this in history books.

statement: Sunlight takes about 8 minutes to reach Earth.
explanation: That's a fact! You can calculate it knowing the speed of light and the distance to the Sun — scientists always confirm the same number.

statement: A message you received says you'll win a free phone if you click a link. Should you believe it?
explanation: Good instinct to question it! These messages are usually scams to steal your data or money. Never click those links by yourself — always show them to a trusted adult first.

statement: If you spend too much time on the computer, your eyes turn square.
explanation: That's a myth and a joke! Spending a lot of time on screens can tire your eyes, but it doesn't change their shape. Still, it's important to take breaks.

title: The Case of the Footprints
scene: Muddy footprints were found in the school hallway leading to the classroom, and the classroom window was open.

clues.text: Big muddy footprints on the floor
A blue backpack next to the door

question: Which clue shows the path of whoever made the floor dirty?
explanation: The footprints are the most direct clue: they show exactly the path of whoever walked in with muddy shoes. The open window or the backpack might have nothing to do with the case.

title: The Mystery of the Wilted Plant
scene: The classroom plant was wilted after the weekend, even though it was watered on Friday before everyone left.

clues.text: The pot was near the window, in strong sun
The soil was dry and cracked
The pot is made of red clay

question: Which clue best explains why the plant wilted?
explanation: The dry, cracked soil shows the water evaporated quickly in the weekend heat. It was the lack of water, not the pot's color, that made the plant wilt.

title: The Misleading Photo
scene: A photo shows a child's hand holding an ice cream that looks gigantic, bigger than their head.

clues.text: The photo was taken very close to the ice cream
You can't see the rest of the child's body in the photo
The ice cream has several colorful scoops

question: Which clue explains why the ice cream looks so gigantic?
explanation: When something is very close to the camera, it looks bigger than it really is. Photos only show part of reality — it's always worth thinking about what's outside the frame.

title: Who Ate the Cake?
setup: The chocolate cake disappeared from the kitchen! There are three suspects.
statements: Tomas was playing ball in the garden all afternoon.
Ines had chocolate around her mouth when mom arrived.
Bobi was sleeping in his bed all day.
question: Who ate the cake?
explanation: Tomas was in the garden and Bobi was sleeping — neither of them could have eaten the cake. Ines had chocolate on her mouth, a clear clue that it was her.

title: Who Broke the Vase?
setup: The living-room vase broke while the parents were at work. There are three suspects.
statements: Whiskers the cat was locked outside all day.
Maria was at school until 5pm, when the vase was still whole.
Pedro was home alone playing ball inside the room.
question: Who broke the vase?
explanation: Whiskers was locked outside and Maria was at school when the vase was still whole — neither could have done it. Only Pedro was home playing ball inside the room.

title: Who Ate the Cookies?
setup: The chocolate cookies disappeared from the jar. There are three suspects.
statements: Grandma doesn't like chocolate cookies and never eats them.
The baby doesn't have teeth yet to eat hard cookies.
The older brother had cookie crumbs in his pocket.
question: Who ate the cookies?
explanation: Grandma doesn't like those cookies and the baby can't chew them — neither could have done it. The crumbs in the older brother's pocket are the clue that gives him away.

title: Is It True? — The Magic Chocolate
claim: A classmate said that if you eat chocolate every day you get super powers.

sourceA.label: A friend from school
sourceA.text: Said they heard it from another friend, but doesn't know where it was confirmed.

sourceB.label: A science book about the human body
sourceB.text: Explains how food affects health, but never mentions super powers.

explanation: A science book is written by experts and carefully reviewed, so it's more reliable than a rumor between friends. When something seems too good to be true, it's worth checking a serious source.

title: Is It True? — The Secret Holiday
claim: A message online says there's no school tomorrow because of a secret holiday.

sourceA.label: A message forwarded by strangers in a group chat
sourceA.text: No one knows who wrote it first or where the information came from.

sourceB.label: The school's official website
sourceB.text: Always publishes the official, confirmed school calendar.

explanation: The school's official website is the source that actually decides the calendar — it's always more reliable than a message that passed through many people and could have changed along the way.

title: Is It True? — The Living Dinosaur
claim: Someone on social media says they saw a living dinosaur in a forest.

sourceA.label: A video with no explanation of where it was filmed
sourceA.text: Shows no evidence or context about the place or date.

sourceB.label: A natural history museum
sourceB.text: Explains that non-avian dinosaurs went extinct millions of years ago, with lots of fossil evidence.

explanation: A science museum is based on lots of evidence studied by experts over many years. A single video, without explanation or context, could easily be a hoax or a trick.

title: AI Got It Wrong — Spider Legs
aiQuestion: How many legs does a spider have?
aiAnswer: A spider has 6 legs, just like an insect.
correctAnswer: A spider has 8 legs — that's why it's not an insect, it's an arachnid.
explanation: The AI got it wrong! Spiders have 8 legs, not 6. Even computers and artificial intelligence can make mistakes, so it's always worth checking against what you already know or a book.

title: AI Got It Wrong — Portugal's Capital
aiQuestion: What is the capital of Portugal?
aiAnswer: The capital of Portugal is Porto.
correctAnswer: The capital of Portugal is Lisbon.
explanation: The AI got it wrong! Portugal's capital is Lisbon, not Porto. Checking important facts in a book, atlas, or with an adult helps catch these mistakes.

title: AI Got It Wrong — Days of the Week
aiQuestion: How many days are in a week?
explanation: The AI got it wrong! A week always has 7 days. It's a good reminder that it's worth thinking for yourself before accepting any answer, even from a computer.
